principles: Fail closed when signed workspace cannot be proven git-backed.
Keep metadata root and signed workspace root explicit rather than inferred.
Preserve CLI Non-authority and Authority Server receipt boundaries.
Avoid arbitrary topology discovery or broad refactors.
drivers: ClawCreek wrapper-root topology makes the current fallback authoritativeCwd unsafe for signed evidence.
review_run_start correctness depends on binding the same workspace that provides HEAD/materialHash.
Future implementation needs a narrow plan with tests before code changes.

options.name: A: Explicit signed workspace binding plan
pros: Fixes the real root mismatch contract.
Can support both local CLI and Authority receipt paths.
cons: Requires adding or documenting a new resolver surface and repair/config path before implementation.

options.name: B: Auto-discover nested git repository
pros: Could make the ClawCreek example work with less operator input.
cons: Violates consistency of logic for host-neutral evidence.

options.name: C: Only improve the error message again
cons: Does not solve end-to-end review_run_start for wrapper-root projects.
Leaves no mechanical path to attach or configure a signed workspace.

chosen: A: Explicit signed workspace binding plan
rationale: Choose explicit signed workspace binding because the observed failure is a correctness contract gap, not a wording problem. The plan should specify fail-closed behavior plus explicit config or attach command before any signing occurs.

preMortem.scenario: Implementation guesses the nested repo automatically.
preMortem.trigger: A wrapper root contains exactly one nested git repo in local testing.
preMortem.consequence: The CLI may later sign the wrong repo in multi-repo projects.
preMortem.mitigation: Require explicit gitRoot config or story worktree attachment; tests cover multiple nested repo ambiguity as fail-closed.

preMortem.scenario: Local reviewer run is described as Authority proof.
preMortem.trigger: Documentation merges host review output and Authority Server language.
preMortem.consequence: DONE or production readiness can be overclaimed without receipts.
preMortem.mitigation: Separate localNonAuthorityAudit from authorityServerPath and require verified gate_decision receipts for Authority claims.

preMortem.scenario: Resolver changes break direct REVIEW compatibility.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation mandates story.worktree for every REVIEW story.
preMortem.consequence: Review-only stories in a normal git-backed project stop working.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep direct REVIEW supported when the metadata root itself is git-backed with HEAD/materialHash.
